learning: Iteration 0 showed off-track exits at bends with max_error near 0.06 m, not oscillation. Sensor span is the first limit to test. Whether the signal scale drop needs more kp, and whether the 0.06 m lead causes lag, are still open.
notes: Geometry follows the Builder's ±0.03 m, 7-sensor proposal. Weights are scaled to the new span, and kp is raised from 2 to 3 to hold the effective steering gain. kd is raised to 0.75 to match.
rationale: Iteration 0 raced: the oval finished 20 of 20 trials, but the s-bend finished only 5 of 20 and the slalom 0 of 20. Both failures were off-track exits (15 and 20 trials). The worst max_error values (0.056 and 0.064) reach the 0.06 m limit, while steering_oscillation stayed modest (0.16 to 0.25) and rms_error was small. The limit is lateral reach at bends, not jitter. The Builder's geometry widens the sensor span to ±0.03 m with 7 sensors at 0.01 m pitch and keeps sensor_size 0.012 m, so footprints still overlap on the 25 mm tape. I kept the geometry exactly as proposed (lead 0.06 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body and mass unchanged) so this race isolates the span effect. Controller: weights are linear across the seven sensors and scaled to the ±2 limit, giving [-2, -4/3, -2/3, 0, 2/3, 4/3, 2]. This signal falls from about 100/m to about 67/m. To keep the effective steering gain (kp × signal scale) near iteration 0's 2 × 100 = 200 per metre, I set kp = 3.0 (3 × 67 ≈ 200). kd rises from 0.5 to 0.75 to keep damping in step with the larger kp. ki stays 0. base_speed stays 1.6 and line_loss stays last_direction, since neither was implicated in the failures. Expected: fewer off-track exits on the s-bend and slalom, with a non-zero slalom finish rate. No result is claimed for this robot.
